title: A List of Names
summaryZh: 娜迪雅帶了一本筆記本到市場,想問清楚客人到底要什麼。她以為答案會跟價錢有關,結果一位老客人講了完全不同的東西。

sentences.text: The following Wednesday, Nadia brought a notebook to the market.
sentences.zh: 下一個星期三,娜迪雅帶了一本筆記本到市場。

sentences.text: It was the cheap kind, with a soft cover and lines that were much too wide.
sentences.zh: 那是最便宜的那種,軟皮封面,格線寬得太多。

sentences.text: She had decided to ask every customer one question before they left.
sentences.zh: 她決定在每位客人離開前問一個問題。

sentences.text: The question was simple: what do you buy that I do not sell?
sentences.zh: 問題很簡單:你會買什麼是我這裡沒有的?

sentences.text: She expected to hear about prices, or about the car park, or about the late hours.
sentences.zh: 她以為聽到的會是價錢、停車場,或是營業到很晚。

sentences.text: By ten o'clock she had written down eleven answers in careful pencil.
sentences.zh: 到了十點,她已經用鉛筆工整地記下十一個答案。

sentences.text: Milk. Rice. Soap. Batteries. Bread. Milk again. Coffee.
sentences.zh: 牛奶。米。肥皂。電池。麵包。又是牛奶。咖啡。

sentences.text: Not one item on the list was anything that she could grow herself.
sentences.zh: 清單上沒有一樣是她自己種得出來的。

sentences.text: She looked at the list and felt the whole idea go quiet inside her.
sentences.zh: 她看著那張清單,覺得整個想法在心裡安靜了下來。

sentences.text: She put the pencil down and looked at the empty half of the market for a while.
sentences.zh: 她放下鉛筆,看著市場空掉的那半邊,看了好一會兒。

sentences.text: Then Mr. Sarr came, as he did every Wednesday, and bought four onions.
sentences.zh: 接著薩爾先生來了,跟每個星期三一樣,買了四顆洋蔥。

sentences.text: He was eighty-one and he always bought exactly four onions and nothing else.
sentences.zh: 他八十一歲,永遠只買四顆洋蔥,別的什麼都不買。

sentences.text: In nine years Nadia had never once thought to ask him why.
sentences.zh: 九年來,娜迪雅從來沒想過要問他為什麼。

sentences.text: She asked him her question, and he did not understand it at first.
sentences.zh: 她問了他那個問題,他一開始沒聽懂。

sentences.text: "What do I buy that you do not sell?" he repeated slowly.
sentences.zh: 「我買什麼是妳這裡沒有的?」他慢慢重複了一遍。

sentences.text: "Nothing. I buy everything else on Monday, at the shop by my house."
sentences.zh: 「沒有。其他東西我星期一在我家旁邊那間店買。」

sentences.text: Nadia did not write anything at all in the notebook.
sentences.zh: 娜迪雅在筆記本上什麼都沒寫。

sentences.text: "Then why do you come here on Wednesday, just for onions?" she asked.
sentences.zh: 「那你為什麼星期三還要來這裡,只買洋蔥?」她問。

sentences.text: Mr. Sarr put his four onions carefully into his bag before he answered.
sentences.zh: 薩爾先生把四顆洋蔥小心地放進袋子,才回答。

sentences.text: He did not seem embarrassed by it, only surprised that she had needed to ask.
sentences.zh: 他看起來一點也不尷尬,只是驚訝她居然需要問。

sentences.text: "Because on Wednesday somebody says my name," he said.
sentences.zh: 「因為星期三會有人叫我的名字,」他說。

sentences.text: "You say it when I arrive, and you say it again when I go."
sentences.zh: 「我來的時候妳叫一次,我走的時候妳再叫一次。」

sentences.text: "Nobody at the shop by my house knows what I am called."
sentences.zh: 「我家旁邊那間店,沒有人知道我叫什麼。」

sentences.text: He said thank you, and he walked away down the empty half of the market.
sentences.zh: 他說了聲謝謝,沿著市場空掉的那半邊走了。

sentences.text: For a moment the only sound was a plastic crate being dragged across the concrete.
sentences.zh: 有那麼一下子,唯一的聲音是塑膠箱在水泥地上拖過的聲音。

sentences.text: Nadia stood behind her crates and did not move for a long time after that.
sentences.zh: 娜迪雅站在箱子後面,之後好長一段時間都沒有動。

sentences.text: She turned the notebook over and looked at the back of the page.
sentences.zh: 她把筆記本翻過來,看著那一頁的背面。

sentences.text: She had been writing down the wrong list for the whole of that morning.
sentences.zh: 她整個早上記的,都是錯的那張清單。

sentences.text: The right list was not a list of goods at all, and never had been.
sentences.zh: 對的那張根本不是商品清單,從來都不是。

sentences.text: It was a list of names, and she already knew every single one of them.
sentences.zh: 那是一張名字的清單,而且她本來就每一個都記得。

sentences.text: That afternoon she wrote them out, one under the other, until the page was full.
sentences.zh: 那天下午,她把名字一個一個寫下來,寫滿了整頁。

sentences.text: Eighty-six names, and beside each one, what that person always bought.
sentences.zh: 八十六個名字,每個名字旁邊寫著那個人固定會買的東西。

sentences.text: Karim found the notebook on the kitchen table that evening.
sentences.zh: 那天傍晚,卡林在廚房桌上看到了那本筆記本。

sentences.text: "This is a customer database," he said. "On paper."
sentences.zh: 「這是客戶資料庫欸,」他說。「紙本的。」

sentences.text: "It is a market," Nadia said. "On paper. Nineteen years of one."
sentences.zh: 「這是一個市場,」娜迪雅說。「紙本的。十九年的市場。」

sentences.text: Karim read the page again, and this time he did not offer to build a website.
sentences.zh: 卡林又把那頁看了一遍,這次他沒有再說要幫她做網站。

sentences.text: Instead he asked her what she wanted to do with it.
sentences.zh: 他反而問她,想拿這個做什麼。

questions.q: What did Nadia expect her customers to talk about?
options: The quality of her tomatoes and onions
The stalls that had already closed down

questions.q: Why does Mr. Sarr come to the market for only four onions?
options: Because someone there uses his name
Because his local shop has no onions on Wednesday
Because Nadia's onions are cheaper than anywhere else

questions.q: What changes in Karim by the end of the day?
options: He stops pushing his own solution and asks what she wants
He decides the market cannot be saved after all
He agrees to leave his job and work at the stall
